page: Amazon Web Services m8i-flex.16xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by the x86_64 architecture. It features an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor with 64 vCPUs, 32 physical cores, and a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor includes a 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and int8 operations, and Intel Total Memory Encryption (TME). This instance does not include local NVMe storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it operates on the Nitro hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 15 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the m8i-flex.16xlarge demonstrates strong multi-core and memory capabilities. It achieves top-tier performance in Geekbench single-core scoring, Geekbench image processing, and static web serving throughput, which reaches 105.74 GB/sec. Multi-core performance is also strong, as evidenced by its stress-ng multi-core score and a Passmark CPU score of 83187.08. Memory read bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 5112.66 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 197.6 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. However, write bandwidth for large blocks and single-core stress-ng performance fall into the average category. The hardware-accelerated AMX instructions contribute to strong prompt processing speeds for large language models, reaching 39.14 tokens/sec on a 70B model, though text generation for the same model is average at 3.52 tokens/sec.

The m8i-flex.16xlarge offers a balanced resource profile, delivering dedicated compute resources and high-speed DDR5 memory without the added cost of bundled local storage or GPUs. This makes it a cost-efficient option for workloads that rely on network-attached storage and do not require hardware acceleration. Tradeoffs include the lack of local SSDs and a moderate baseline network speed of 15 Gbps. This instance is suited for workloads such as static web serving, database operations, software compilation, and medium-scale LLM inference tasks.
